record.original_question: Is the completeness or the uniqueness undecidable, when context-freeF -factorizations are given by deterministic automata or by linear context-free grammars?

evidence.quote: Is the completeness or the uniqueness undecidable, when context-freeF -factorizations are given by deterministic automata or by linear context-free grammars?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions. Let $A$ be a finite alphabet and let $A^*$ denote the free monoid of finite words over $A$. A factorization of a word $w \in A^*$ is a sequence $(u_1, u_2, \dots, u_k)$ of words $u_i \in A^*$ such that $w = u_1 u_2 \cdots u_k$. Fix a language $F \subseteq A^*$ (the "factor language"). An $F$-factorization of a word $w$ is a factorization $(u_1, \dots, u_k)$ in which every factor $u_i$ belongs to $F$.

Say that the language $F$ is:
 - complete (with respect to $F$-factorizations) if every word of $A^*$ admits at least one $F$-factorization;
 - unique (with respect to $F$-factorizations) if every word of $A^*$ admits at most one $F$-factorization.

Call $F$ a context-free $F$-factorization language when $F$ is a context-free language. Two natural restricted ways of presenting $F$ are:
 (i) by a deterministic (pushdown) automaton recognizing $F$;
 (ii) by a linear context-free grammar generating $F$.

Problem. Determine whether each of the following decision problems is decidable or undecidable.

(a) Given a context-free language $F \subseteq A^*$ presented by a deterministic pushdown automaton, decide whether $F$ is complete; and separately, decide whether $F$ is unique.

(b) Given a context-free language $F \subseteq A^*$ presented by a linear context-free grammar, decide whether $F$ is complete; and separately, decide whether $F$ is unique.

In other words: is completeness undecidable, and is uniqueness undecidable, in each of the settings (i) and (ii)?

artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not turn up any specific decidability or undecidability result for completeness or uniqueness of context-free $F$-factorizations when $F$ is given by a deterministic pushdown automaton or by a linear context-free grammar. General undecidability results for context-free grammars (universality, ambiguity, equivalence) are known, but they do not directly settle this restricted question. No source confirming a resolution was located, so the status is recorded as unknown.

status_evidence.title: Undecidable Problems for Context-free Grammars (Hoogeboom)
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys classical undecidability results for context-free grammars, including ambiguity and universality, but does not address F-factorization completeness/uniqueness.
status_evidence.claim: Standard undecidability results for CFGs are documented, yet none specifically resolves completeness/uniqueness for context-free F-factorizations under the stated restricted presentations.

status_evidence.title: Deterministic context-free grammar — Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Describes deterministic CFLs and decidable problems (e.g., equivalence of DPDAs).
status_evidence.claim: Some problems are decidable for DPDAs, but completeness/uniqueness of F-factorizations is not discussed.
